stories.title: Agility Robotics now expects to raise about $465 million as it goes public through a SPAC merger
paragraphs: Humanoid robot maker Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI said on Oct. 30, 2026 that they expect Agility to raise about $465 million through its proposed merger with the special-purpose acquisition company, The Robot Report reports. According to Agility, that total includes about $164 million from Churchill XI's trust account, about $201 million from a common stock private investment led by Foxconn at $10 per share, and $100 million in equity funding already received after the deal was announced.

The Robot Report notes that the total is less than the $620 million Agility predicted, at a $2.5 billion valuation, when it first announced the planned combination in June. Agility expects the deal to close on Nov. 4, subject to shareholder approval and customary conditions, and said on X that it expects to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT on Nov. 5. The Salem, Oregon company has said it will be the first U.S. publicly traded, pure-play humanoid supplier with commercial deployments.

According to The Robot Report, Agility unveiled its Digit 5 humanoid last month and says it is on track to begin deliveries to early-access customers in the first half of 2027, with general availability targeted for the end of 2027. The company says it has more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5. In a September filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Agility reported $1.8 million in net sales in 2025, with customers across nine sites including Toyota, Mercado Libre and Schaeffler.
